idea-plugin.name: Micrometer Timer Sample Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning icon on a Micrometer Timer.Sample sample = Timer.start(...) whose declaring method never calls .stop(...) on that sample anywhere -- Micrometer's own reference docs show the sample usage as exactly two steps, start then stop, with no mention of a try/finally guard. A sample that's started but never stopped never records its timing, and per a real upstream Micrometer issue, can leak in long-task-timer bookkeeping if this happens repeatedly.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches method/variable names by simple text, so it works whether the real Micrometer jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: v0.1 flags only the fully-unambiguous case -- .stop(...) is never called on the variable anywhere in the method, not even inside a branch. If .stop(...) is called on any path (even one that doesn't cover every branch), this is NOT flagged -- true control-flow/exception-path analysis is out of scope for v0.1.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
